mechanism: Bit 0 of the counter is the parity of the block: the block's left end oscillates between two fixed cells for a whole phase and only its right end erodes. The counter word L lives in K = words whose 1-runs all have length >= 2; K is closed under the visit, nothing in it halts inside a phase, and the block change is exact (d = -1 / -3 by block parity, d = r-1 when the final gap is 1 and the bottom run r merges). So m mod 4 in {1,2} (the sync) can only break at a merge. If the final gap z is >= 3 at an even visit, z alternates exactly '=3' / '>=4' for the rest of the phase and no merge happens. The reset maps z to z-1 and n' = 4 visits + 2. In the steady class (n = 6 mod 8, z = 3 at start, long bottom run) this closes: visits = 3 mod 4, z_reset = 4, z' = 3, n' = 6 mod 8. The real run is in that class from phase 11 on. Deepen2: inside a phase the counter is a binary counter on fixed cells (bit 1 = right end of the bottom run, bit 2 = its left end). From phase 15 the bottom run loses exactly 1 cell per phase; it becomes an 11 digit at phases 91 and 119, and both times a 3-phase excursion (z_reset 8, then z 7 > 3, then z 2 with one merge, d = +1) restores the steady class. Excursions are safe when the run that becomes the bottom is long; runs of 3-4 arriving during an excursion go off-sync (random tests 9/40). Follow stage: a C port of the jump simulator followed the real orbit to phase 1,857 (n ~ 2^1860) with no off-sync; excursions at phases 91, 119, 215, 487 were all benign, and after each one a merge wave climbs from the bottom (about 0.5 runs per phase), absorbing short runs (the 3-run from phase 171 was absorbed at phase 231-233) and leaving a frozen, ever coarser low region. A fast-forward check (exact on the past excursion) predicts the next excursion at phase 3,321 as benign.

rounds.model: State (L, m, g): L in K, m = block, g = pad (always 0 mod 4). Visit: (L,m,g) -> (inc L, m+d(L,m), g+4); reset at m=2: n' = g+6. Invariants: S (m mod 4 in {1,2}), P (final gap alternates 3 / >=4 once >=3), R (z_start = z_reset - 1). Steady class Sigma = {n = 6 mod 8, z_start = 3, bottom run never an erasable 11 digit}.

rounds.model: Per phase: fixed-cell binary counter (N0 = 3) on a layout P; phase map P -> P' driven by the final counter value (n+2 = omega x 2^j, omega odd, changed by +1 at each excursion merge). Bottom run r: r' = r - 1 per phase; at r = 2 a 3-phase excursion makes the next run the bottom (minus 2). Safety lemma B': no run of length <= 4 becomes the bottom during an excursion.

rounds.model: Phase map on the counter word, as run lengths a0 (bottom), a1, ... with gaps. Steady phase: a0 -> a0 - 1, everything else frozen below the wave front. Excursion when a0 = 2: a1 becomes the bottom (minus 2), 3-phase sync pattern, then a merge wave climbs from the bottom at ~0.5 runs per phase (gap 3 -> 2, then merge), absorbing short runs and leaving the low region frozen behind it. Candidate maturation rule M: the cascade's first merges always produce the new bottom and the new a1, so a1 >= 6 at every excursion.
